title: fix(plugin-dashboard): read a field's format as a date pattern only on date/datetime fields
body:
Fixes #10220

## What changed

`renderFieldValue` (`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/recordFields.tsx`, behind the dashboard `object-data-table` cells and `RecordDetailDrawer`) sent any `format` containing one of the letters Y / M / D / H / m / s to `formatDate`, whatever the field type. Its date branch now also requires the field's type to be `date` or `datetime`, through a new unexported `DATE_PATTERN_FIELD_TYPES` set placed beside `NUMERIC_FIELD_TYPES`. Date and datetime fields render exactly as before. Every other field falls through to the cell renderer its type and `format` hint select. The currency and percent branches ahead of it are untouched.

## Measured on the unfixed tree (`8b1f06619`)

The card's relayed probe, now run first-hand, plus the other cases the census found. Every case goes through the real `renderFieldValue` with `en-US`:

| field | value | painted before | painted after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` + `format: 'email'` (the card's probe, built by `buildFieldMeta`) | `ada@example.com` | em dash | mailto link |
| `text` + `format: 'money'` | `1234.5` | `Jan 1, 1970` | currency face containing `1,234.50` |
| no type + `format: 'email'` | `ada@example.com` | em dash | mailto link |
| `autonumber` + `format: 'ORD-{YYYYMMDD}-{00}'` | `ORD-20240315-01` | em dash | `ORD-20240315-01` |
| `time` + `format: 'HH:mm'` | `14:30` | em dash | `14:30` |
| CONTROL `date` + `format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'` | `2020-03-04T12:00:00.000Z` | `Mar 4, 2020` | `Mar 4, 2020` |
| CONTROL `datetime` + `format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm'` | same | `Mar 4, 2020` | `Mar 4, 2020` |

One-off probes on the same unfixed tree also painted an em dash for `text` + `format: 'short'` and `text` + `format: 'markdown'`. Those two are not pinned and were not re-measured after the change.

## Route: gate on the field type, not a hint-word exclusion list

- **B2:** `fieldMeta.type` is present at the branch. `buildFieldMeta` writes `type: overrides.type ?? meta?.type`, which is the member `resolveCellRendererType(fieldMeta)` reads on the next line.
- **B1 census:** which field types reach `renderFieldValue` with a date-pattern `format` today?
  - objectstack `examples/**` at `2c1011b`: zero `format` keys on object fields. The `format` hits there are dataset measures, widget options and one validation rule (`format: 'email'`). Zero formulas with `returnType: 'date'` and zero autonumber date-token patterns, including under `packages/**`.
  - objectui tree: the only date-pattern input to `renderFieldValue` outside this PR is the `DATE` fixture in `dashboardFaces.displayLocale-9909.test.tsx`. It is a type-less `FieldMeta` literal whose test covers locale plumbing. The README's `close_date` example column gets its type (`date`) from the bound object schema.
  - Docs that teach a date-letter `format` on a non-date type: `content/docs/fields/auto-number.mdx` (`{YYYY}-{0000}`, `ORD-{YYYYMMDD}-{00}`). These are collisions, not something that relies on the branch.
  - Result: no non-date type relies on the branch. The type route loses nothing that was measured. It also fixes the autonumber and time collisions, which a hint-word list would miss.
  - One case could rely on the branch, but none exists today: a `formula` field whose `format` is a date pattern. The old tree painted it `Mar 4, 2020`; it now paints the raw value through `FormulaCellRenderer`, which is what the list view already paints. `FieldMeta` does not carry `returnType`, and the census found no such producer. Adding a member for it would grow `ObjectDataTable`'s derived override bands for a case nobody uses, so it is left out.
- **Four axes:**
  - Real business need: the census found nothing that needs non-date fields formatted as dates. Hint words and autonumber patterns are documented authoring.
  - Long-run soundness: the resolver's vocabulary stays the only list of hint words. The `FieldSchema.format` description in objectstack#19763 already keys `format` by field type.
  - Guarding against AI authoring errors: a hint word written on a text field now reaches the renderer it names instead of making the value disappear. A type-less column has to declare `type: 'date'`; letters in its format no longer imply a date.
  - No scope spread: no new exported surface, no new `FieldMeta` member, no new gate.
- **Declared cost:** a dashboard table column with an unknown type (no object-schema field and no `type` on the column) is no longer date-formatted from its `format` alone. Declaring `TableColumn.type: 'date'` brings the date face back; a case pins this.

## Fixture triage

`dashboardFaces.displayLocale-9909.test.tsx` adds `type: 'date'` to its `DATE` FieldMeta (add-declaration disposition). Measured on the fix without that key: all four `date-format branch` cases turn red (4 failed, 8 passed of 12). The fixture only omitted the type because the old branch never read it.

## Tests (final head `a688648bc`)

- New `recordFields.formatHintNotDatePattern-10220.test.tsx`, 8 cases. On the unfixed tree the first seven-case version gave 4 failed and 3 passed (the email, money, type-less email and autonumber cases were red; the three controls were green). The time case was added after a one-off probe measured its em dash on the same tree.
- Ablation after committing the fix: `ablation-replace.mjs` deleted the `DATE_PATTERN_FIELD_TYPES.has(...)` line (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed). Result: 5 failed, 3 passed, with exactly the five non-date cases red and the controls green. Restored: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The subject is imported by relative path from `src`, so no `dist` step is involved.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/` on `a688648bc`: 122 files and 1159 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) passed on `a688648bc`, after building the 13-package dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-dashboard^...'`). A `--listFiles` check confirmed the test program includes both touched test files.
- Changeset and repo gates on `a688648bc`, each exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check-control-bytes`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the four paths returns NOT GOVERNED.
- Lint, narrowed to the three touched ts/tsx files (declared):
  1. Population, read from eslint's own config: `--print-config` on each file shows 96 active rules and no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`. The ts block extends the non-type-checked `tseslint.configs.recommended`.
  2. Count, from `--format json`: 3 files, 0 errors, 15 warnings. All 15 are `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` in `recordFields.tsx`, and the base blob of that file gives the same 15.
  3. Invariance: type-aware linting is off, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.

NOT MEASURED: repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` shards (both CI's). `Spec Main Shape Gate` is red on every head per objectui#10287 and is not part of this change.

## Acceptance notes

- A `datetime` field with a `format` keeps the date-only `formatDate` face, while one without a `format` uses `DateTimeCellRenderer` (date and time). That behavior predates this change, which leaves it as is.
- The `TableColumn.format` docstring in `packages/types` says the key is honoured by the currency / percent / date branches of `renderFieldValue`. That is still true, but it does not say the date branch now depends on the column type. The docstring is outside this PR's file surface; the seat can add one clause if it wants.
- `check-changeset-claims` lists three pending changesets that name `recordFields.tsx` (`5876-one-lookup-predicate`, `6874-retire-titleformat`, `dashboard-expandable-family-convergence-5692`). They cover `isLookupType`, `titleFormat` and the expandable family, none of which this diff touches, so they remain true.
